models_evaluated: commercial AI software for pulmonary nodule assessment (unnamed)

links.outcome: Radiologist report completion time before versus after AI implementation (operational outcome, not patient outcomes)
links.effect: Adjusted HR 1.17 (95% CI 1.14, 1.21); median reporting time fell from 21.3 to 18.2 minutes (14.6% reduction); emergency department exams increased 7.1%. Patient outcomes and safety not assessed.
links.quote: AI implementation was associated with faster report completion (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.17; 95% CI: 1.14, 1.21; P < .001).

links.outcome: Operational metric (reporting time) and projected workforce and financial impact after AI deployment
links.effect: Median reporting time decreased 21.3 to 18.2 minutes (14.6%); exploratory modeling suggested about 0.5 FTE radiologist workload reduction at institutional volumes.
links.quote: At institutional scan volumes (approximately 20 000-22 000 chest CT examinations annually), exploratory modeling suggested an approximate reduction of 0.5 full-time equivalent radiologist workload.

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating the real-world deployment impact of commercial AI on radiologist reading and reporting times pre- vs post-implementation, without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
